clinician.final_diagnosis: Histopathology revealed an adenocarcinoma with HER2 overexpression (immuohistochemical score 3+)
clinician.trajectory_summary: The patient presented with mild and intermittent left upper quadrant discomfort and leukocytosis. Initial hematological workup ruled out myeloproliferative neoplasms. CT imaging subsequently revealed significant wall thickening at the gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) with a nodular abnormality in the proximal stomach and multiple hypodensities in the liver. An EGD further identified a fungating mass at the GEJ. Despite multiple attempts to retrieve the specific pathology report, the system did not provide the histopathological confirmation of adenocarcinoma and HER2 overexpression.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with mild and intermittent discomfort in the left upper quadrant (LUQ) and leukocytosis (total leukocyte count of 25 600/uL with absolute neutrophil of 21 000/uL)
Initial hematological workup, including peripheral smear, JAK2 V617F mutation, and BCR/ABL, revealed no evidence of leukemia or other myeloproliferative neoplasms
CT chest/abdomen/pelvis showed significant wall thickening at the GEJ with a nodular abnormality projecting into the proximal stomach and multiple hypodensities of the liver
EGD revealed a fungating mass at the GEJ without active bleeding
